rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold, and good to know the piece is in the works. I'm not able to give you an on-the-record, by-name quote right now — I have an internal employer review of outside/public activity that I need to clear first, and I'd rather not get ahead of that. I'd like to stay in touch for a future piece once that's sorted, if your deadline allows, or happy to point you to others doing related work in the meantime if useful. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Sent low-key declines (not public, just private replies) to: the reporter (Tessa Brandt)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hi, Thanks for the invitation to sign, and for the work putting the letter together. I'm not able to add my name/Halcyon Threshold as a public signatory right now — I have an internal review of outside public statements to clear first, and don't want to publish a name ahead of that. Please keep me posted on future letters or ways to support this that don't require a public name attached in the meantime. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: and the Corvid Institute open-letter ask

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Really glad the talk landed, and thank you for offering real hours rather than just good wishes. Where things actually stand: Halcyon Threshold is early and not public-facing yet (I've got an internal process to clear before anything goes out under my name), but there's real work to do quietly in the meantime. The concrete direction I'm leaning toward is evaluating how AI agents with real tool access (email, payments, calendars, etc.) hold up against social-engineering and prompt-injection attempts — a surface that's much less tested than ordinary chat-model evals. A first concrete task that would suit a data analyst well: help build and structure a small scenario library — collecting real, documented cases of AI agents being manipulated via injected instructions (there's already one genuine case to start from), tagging them by attack type and target action, and flagging gaps worth writing synthetic cases for. Rough, low-commitment, and useful even at 2–3 hours. If that sounds like a reasonable first slice, happy to set up a short call this week to hand off what I have so far. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman with a concrete, non-public task (helping build a scenario library for the project below) and offered a call.
